name: multi_timeframe_confirmation_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Using 1-min bars for entry but requiring confirmation from a 5-min or 15-min signal reduces noise dramatically. When a 5-min EMA crossover fires (EMA_9 > EMA_21 on 5-min bars) AND the 1-min RSI(7) is oversold (< 25), you're entering a 5-min trend on a 1-min pullback. The higher timeframe confirms direction; the lower timeframe optimizes entry. Edge persists because most traders use a single timeframe and either get poor entries (higher TF only) or poor direction (lower TF only).
mechanism: Multiple independent signals confirming the same direction increase the probability that a genuine order flow imbalance exists, not just noise. When momentum, volume, and volatility signals align, it indicates that institutional activity is creating measurable market impact across multiple dimensions simultaneously, increasing the confidence of directional prediction.
weaknesses: 5-min trend can lag — by the time EMA crossover fires on 5-min, the 1-min move may be mostly done
RSI(7) < 25 on 1-min during a 5-min uptrend is an aggressive pullback — might be the start of a reversal, not a pullback
Maintaining two timeframe calculations adds implementation complexity
prior_art: Multi-timeframe trading — Alexander Elder (Triple Screen). Systematic implementation.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
